# QuickMessage — Native Text Expander for macOS

> QuickMessage is an ultra-fast, lightweight, and privacy-first native text expander and snippet manager engineered specifically for macOS and Apple Silicon.

## Overview
QuickMessage runs quietly in the macOS Menu Bar and expands short keyboard shortcuts (such as `\bank`, `\email`, `\sig`, or custom triggers) into full snippets, email templates, code blocks, and formatted text across every macOS app without keystroke delay.

Unlike traditional text expanders built with web wrappers or Electron, QuickMessage is built natively with a high-performance Rust core and Swift AppKit interface. It consumes under 20MB of RAM, incurs 0% idle CPU usage, and executes snippet matching completely offline.

## Core Features & Capabilities
- **Keystroke Expansion**: Automatically detects shortcut triggers (default prefix `\`) and expands them instantly in any active application (Slack, Apple Mail, Telegram, VS Code, Notion, Google Docs, Safari, Chrome, etc.).
- **Fuzzy Search Popover**: Type the trigger prefix `\` to summon a floating, lightweight fuzzy-search window to find and insert snippets using arrow keys and Enter.
- **Dynamic Variables & Fill-in Fields**: Supports dynamic template placeholders (e.g. current date, time, clipboard contents, custom cursor positions) for interactive forms and automated replies.
- **End-to-End Encrypted iCloud Sync**: Automatically synchronizes snippets across all your Mac devices using your personal Apple iCloud (CloudKit Private Database). No secondary accounts, logins, or vendor servers required.
- **macOS Native Manager**: A clean, native macOS window to organize snippets into categories, search, customize triggers, and export/import JSON backups.
- **AI Prompt Accelerator**: Ideal for quick insertion of complex ChatGPT, Claude, and LLM master prompts and code review templates into AI web chat and developer tools.

## Performance Benchmarks
- **Memory Footprint**: < 20 MB RAM (over 90% lighter than Electron-based expanders).
- **Expansion Latency**: < 1 ms response time from keystroke trigger to text replacement.
- **Background CPU**: 0.0% idle CPU usage. Completely eliminates background battery drain.
- **Architecture**: Native 64-bit ARM binary built for Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4 and newer).

## Privacy & Security Architecture
- **100% Local Keystroke Matching**: All keystroke detection is processed entirely in local memory on your Mac. Keystrokes are never logged to disk, never recorded, and never transmitted over the internet.
- **Zero Third-Party Cloud Servers**: QuickMessage has no external telemetry, tracking, or analytics backend.
- **Apple Keychain Encryption**: Local databases are protected by encryption keys generated on install and stored directly in the macOS Keychain.
- **Apple CloudKit**: Cloud synchronization operates strictly within the user's private Apple iCloud container, inheriting Apple's end-to-end security model.
- **Minimal Permissions**: Requires only standard macOS Accessibility permission solely to detect configured shortcut prefixes and insert expanded text into the active focused app.

## Comparison with Alternatives
- **vs TextExpander**: QuickMessage is a native Apple Silicon app with no monthly or annual subscription fees (TextExpander costs ~$40/year). It uses under 20MB of RAM vs 250MB–450MB on TextExpander, and syncs via personal Apple iCloud rather than proprietary third-party servers.
- **vs aText**: QuickMessage features a modern Swift/Rust architecture optimized for recent macOS versions (Sonoma, Sequoia), zero legacy baggage, native iCloud CloudKit synchronization, and Mac App Store sandboxed security.
- **vs Alfred Snippets**: QuickMessage provides a dedicated standalone Menu Bar tool with real-time popup suggestions (`\`) without requiring Alfred Powerpack purchase or complex workflow configurations.

## Pricing & Availability
- **Pricing**: Free to download for macOS (.dmg installer).
- **Platform**: macOS 13.0 (Ventura) or later.
- **Hardware**: Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2/M3/M4 or newer).
